sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of PC and Console Video Games via Digital Stores

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (unitary national jurisdiction; no separate sub-state corporate register)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law - codified French statutory tradition (Napoleonic code lineage), supplemented by directly applicable EU supranational regulations and directives
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-United States Double Taxation Convention (signed 31 Aug. 1994, amended by Protocol of 13 Jan. 2009)
France-China Double Taxation Agreement (signed 26 Nov. 2013, in force since 20 Dec. 2014)
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisionally applied since 21 Sep. 2017)
EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement (provisionally applied since 1 Jan. 2021)
France-Japan Double Taxation Convention (signed 1995, updated by the 2017 Protocol)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (France), Articles L. 223-1 to L. 223-43 (SARL formation and governance), Article L. 123-36 et seq. (Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises), Articles R. 123-1 to R. 123-12 (RCS registration), Decree n° 84-406 (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés procedural rules), Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (Digital Services Act) as applicable to online intermediation transparency.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Registry of the Commercial Court) in the territorial jurisdiction of the registered office, interfaced through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form M0 (immatriculation d'une personne morale) filed electronically through the Guichet Unique; the constitutive instrument is the 'Statuts constitutifs' (Articles of Association), and the post-registration certificate is the 'K-bis' extract issued by the Greffe.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for a SARL under Article L. 223-2 of the Code de commerce; the Articles may fix capital at any freely determined amount, commonly between 1 EUR and 1,000 EUR. Where capital is 10,000 EUR or more, only 20% of cash contributions must be blocked and paid up at subscription, with the balance payable within five years. Where capital is below 10,000 EUR, 100% of cash contributions must be fully blocked and paid up before registration. Cash contributions must be deposited in a French credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations on a dedicated blocked account in the name of the company in formation; funds are released to the Gérant only after RCS registration. Non-cash contributions (apports en nature) must be fully released at subscription and, in principle, valued by a commissaire aux apports.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the founding associates of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée hereby adopt the Company's Articles of Association and acknowledge that the subscribed share capital of €1,000 has been fully subscribed and paid in, with each subscriber's contribution recorded in the subscription list. RESOLVED FURTHER: that the registered office be established at the address stated in the Articles, and that the Gérant be authorised to complete registration before the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés. RESOLVED FINALLY: that [Named Person], having accepted office, is appointed Gérant for an unlimited term, with full powers to manage the Company, open bank accounts, sign publishing and platform agreements with Steam and PlayStation Store operators, and perform any and all ancillary formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the Articles of Association (Statuts) and allocation of share subscriptions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding associates acting by private deed (acte sous seing privé) or before a notary ('Maître') if authentication is chosen; no notarial deed is mandatory unless a real-estate contribution is made.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding associates prepare the statuts in compliance with Articles L. 223-1 and L. 223-7 of the Code de commerce, including all mandatory particulars: corporate name, legal form (SARL), registered office address, corporate purpose (publishing, distribution and marketing of videogames for PC and consoles through digital stores such as Steam and PlayStation Store), duration up to 99 years, share capital amount and division, rights attached to shares, identity of the Gérant, and the valuation procedure for any non-cash contribution. Each associate must sign every page and the final signature page; the designated Gérant must also sign the acceptance of office. If non-cash contributions are made, a commissaire aux apports must issue a valuation report before the deed is finalised.
required_dossiers: Draft statuts signed by all associates
Subscription list with surname, first name, date and place of birth, nationality, address and number of shares of each associate
Passport or national identity card of each associate and of the prospective Gérant
Valuation report of the commissaire aux apports (only where non-cash contributions exist)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the commissaire aux apports or the notary refuses to authenticate or issues a reservation, the associates must amend the valuation basis or re-characterise the contribution in cash, and then re-execute the statuts in full.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocking of the share capital deposit with a French credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank (établissement de crédit) or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC); the account is opened in the name of the SARL 'en formation'.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Each cash contribution is transferred to a blocked account opened for the company in formation. The bank issues a deposit certificate (certificat du dépositaire or attestation de blocage de fonds) stating the exact amount held and the blocked purpose. Where the total capital is below 10,000 EUR, the full cash amount must be blocked and paid up at subscription; where the capital is 10,000 EUR or higher, at least 20% must be deposited now and the balance made payable within five years. The certificate must be preserved and attached to the registration file; the funds are released to the Gérant only after the K-bis extract is issued.
required_dossiers: Draft statuts of the company in formation
Identity documents of each associate and the legal representative
Bank KYC forms including the source of funds and beneficial ownership information
Signed power of attorney if a third party is instructed to open the account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account opening on KYC or source-of-funds grounds, the associates must provide supplementary proof of identity and provenance of funds; if the refusal persists, the deposit may be made with another licensed bank or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of the incorporation docket through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, in liaison with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office jurisdiction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The legal representative creates an account on the Guichet Unique and selects the creation of a commercial SARL; the platform generates the M0 form. The following documents are attached: the signed statuts, the bank deposit certificate, identity documents of the Gérant, the declaration of non-conviction and absence of insolvency bar for the Gérant, proof of occupation of the registered office (lease, accommodation certificate or title deed), and the beneficial ownership declaration (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs) with civil identity, nationality and percentage of control of each beneficial owner. The INPI verifies formal completeness and dispatches the file to the RCS, URSSAF, DGFIP and INSEE for parallel processing.
required_dossiers: Signed statuts (PDF)
Certificat du dépositaire or attestation de blocage de fonds
Passport of the Gérant and declaration of no criminal or insolvency bar
Proof of registered office occupation (lease, titre de propriété or attestation de domiciliation)
Beneficial ownership declaration (RBE) with supporting identity documents of each beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique or the Greffe issues a motivated rejection (rejet), the depositor is notified in the online dashboard; the file may be supplemented or corrected within the procedural window, generally 15 days, and resubmitted without necessarily re-paying the full filing fee if the original fee covers the formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the RCS and issuance of the K-bis extract and statistical identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) and INSEE (Institut National de la Statistique et des Études Économiques).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon confirmation of compliance, the Greffe registers the SARL and issues the certificate of incorporation (K-bis extract) which constitutes the official proof of legal existence. The K-bis states the SIREN, SIRET, the principal activity code 5820Z (software publishing), legal form, share capital, registered office and the identity of the Gérant. INSEE assigns the national identifiers and the company is allocated a VAT number; the registration is published in the BODACC in electronic form.
required_dossiers: Registration dossier reference number received from the Guichet Unique
Payment confirmation of the applicable registration taxes and greffe fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis extract contains errors in the APE code, capital amount, registered office or officer details, a formal demand for rectification (demande de rectification) must be filed with the Greffe, supported by the relevant pages of the statuts; the correction is generally processed within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration operational formalities: social security, insurance, VAT, and platform enrolment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF (social security), DGFIP (VAT and corporate income tax), the insurance brokerage market, and the private storefront operator portals (Steamworks and PlayStation Partner Program).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Gérant must be registered with URSSAF under the assisted employee social security regime (assimilé salarié); the company is automatically registered with DGFIP for VAT and income tax. Professional civil liability insurance covering commercial publishing activities is subscribed. For the digital activity, the company enrols in the Steamworks Publisher Agreement (Valve) and the PlayStation Partner Program, providing payout bank details and tax documentation. The company must ensure compliance with Regulation (EU) 2019/1150 (Platform-to-Business) regarding transparency of ranking and account suspension, and must provide the storefronts with an PEGI age rating for each game title, together with a privacy policy compliant with Regulation (EU) 2016/679.
required_dossiers: K-bis extract and statuts
RBE receipt from the Guichet Unique
IBAN and bank account details in the corporate name
Tax identification and VAT number for payout forms
PEGI rating certificate or questionnaire for each published title
Privacy policy and end-user terms compliant with Regulation (EU) 2016/679
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If URSSAF rejects the manager registration or the platform refuses the payout account, verify the SWIFT/IBAN ownership and re-submit corrected tax forms; for platform rejection, align the content rating and privacy documentation, then resubmit the storefront enrolment application.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - the activity is a dematerialised digital publishing service (ISIC 5820, software publishing) and no industrial establishment or classified installation subject to the ICPE regime (Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement) is operated; market access is governed by private storefront contracts (Steamworks, PlayStation Partner Program) and the PEGI age-rating system.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - French law does not require a State operating licence for videogame digital publishing; compulsory compliance arises from the Digital Services Act, consumer protection and data protection rules rather than from a sectoral industrial permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable - DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) has no jurisdiction in the absence of an ICPE-classified establishment; the activity involves zero physical production.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no environmental impact assessment or prior notice (étude d'impact) is required for a dematerialised software publishing activity; there are no industrial effluent, VOC emissions, or aqueous waste streams.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - no discharge points exist; only standard municipal waste from the registered office is generated, and the annual corporate emissions reporting obligation is not triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for manufacturing. For the registered office, the Gérant must ensure general workplace safety under Articles L. 4121-1 et seq. of the Code du travail, including fire extinguishing equipment and adequate first-aid measures. If the offices are open to the public, the ERP regime (établissement recevant du public) under the Code de la construction et de l'habitation would require a fire safety certificate and a commission de sécurité visit; no such permit is needed for a closed back-office digital publishing operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) for corporate income tax, VAT, withholding taxes and overall French tax administration; filings are made via the impots.gouv.fr professional portal (Espace Professionnel). Business registration and statutory filings are initiated through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr. VAT non-resident registration is handled by the DGFiP Non-Résidents Tax Service (Service des Impôts des Entreprises – Etrangers Résidents Non-Résidents).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A newly formed French SARL obtains its statutory TIN through the one-stop business registration platform: the legal representative files the creation dossier with the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr). INSEE then assigns the SIREN (9-digit identification number) and SIRET (14-digit establishment number); DGFiP simultaneously issues the French VAT intra-Community number (numéro d'identification TVA intracommunautaire, format FR + a two-digit key + SIREN) and the corporate tax account number (numéro de gestion). A non-resident entity with no French establishment and no fixed place of business in France that makes taxable supplies in France must register for VAT using the simplified non-resident registration procedure: complete and file form 1475-SD (or 3550-SD for the special OSS registration) with the DGFiP Non-Résidents Service, providing corporate constitutional documents, evidence of foreign tax registration, and proof of identity of the legal representative; if the foreign entity is established outside the EU/EEA and has no EU intermediary, it must appoint a French tax representative (représentant fiscal) jointly responsible for VAT collection. No French residence or local partner is required for a foreign-owned SARL; the minimum capital requirement has been abrogated, though statutory and article-of-association capital must be stated in the registered deeds.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SARL is by default subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) under Article 206 CGI, and there is no general US-style check-the-box election. Statutory elections available are: (i) the 'SARL de famille' pass-through election under Article 239 bis AA CGI, available only when all partners are natural persons belonging to the same family, where the company may opt to be taxed as an income-tax partnership (impôt sur le revenu) unless an IS option is exercised; (ii) the reverse option to corporate income tax by entities that would otherwise be fiscally transparent, pursuant to Articles 206 and 239 bis A CGI; (iii) the French VAT group election (assujettis uniques) under Articles 1693 ter and 267 quinquies CGI, allowing a French legal entity and its closely held foreign or domestic establishments to form a single VAT taxable person; and (iv) tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI, requiring 95% or greater shareholding in French subsidiaries, separately available for corporate income tax purposes. Hybrid mismatch elections are governed by EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) rules transposed into Articles 212 bis and 209 CGI, and do not permit elective entity classification outside the statutory corporate law forms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established SARL, VAT registration is mandatory from the first taxable transaction; there is no general turnover threshold for ordinary taxable persons. The small-enterprise VAT exemption (franchise en base de TVA) under Article 293 B CGI applies only to French-established businesses whose annual turnover does not exceed €85,000 for supplies of goods, €37,500 for supplies of services, and €85,000 for certain low-margin businesses, provided the supply is not within hotel, catering, transport, or other excluded sectors; as soon as the applicable threshold is exceeded, registration becomes compulsory. Non-resident suppliers without French establishment generally have no registration threshold and are required to register in France from the first taxable French transaction, except where EU special schemes (OSS/IOSS for distance sales of goods and electronically supplied services) permit a single EU registration; the EU-wide €10,000 annual threshold applies only to intra-EU distance sales of goods and services for suppliers established in a Member State, and registration in France is required immediately if the threshold is exceeded or if the supplier opts into a French registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has enacted a mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting regime for all domestic B2B transactions and B2C transaction reporting, replacing the previous derogatory acceptance of paper/PDF invoices. Under Articles 289 bis, 289 quinquies and 289 septies CGI, a French-established VAT taxpayer must issue structured e-invoices and transmit invoice data to the DGFiP through one of two channels: the public free portal (Portail Public de Facturation, PPF) or a certified private dematerialization partner platform (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire, PDP) exposed via REST APIs using a secure token. E-invoices must comply with either Factur-X (EN 16931-compliant structured hybrid) or EDI format (EDIFACT/custom EDI conforming to EN 16931). The mandatory transmission flows phase in from 1 September 2026 for large and medium-sized enterprises (grandes entreprises and ETI) and from 1 September 2027 for SMEs and microenterprises. France does not currently operate a real-time fiscal clearance model requiring pre-approval or cryptographic digital stamping before invoice issuance; instead, the PPF and PDPs provide continuous transaction control by near-real-time structured data exchange, with a monthly aggregation to DGFiP for VAT reporting. B2C sales of digital gaming content are subject to e-reporting (identification of the customer, transaction amounts, VAT rate) even when no structured e-invoice is required; OSS returns for EU-wide B2C digital services are filed quarterly electronically. Non-established suppliers without French establishment that use OSS are not subject to the French B2B e-invoicing mandate for their B2C OSS sales, but all domestic B2B transactions requiring French VAT must flow through e-invoicing channels if the supplier has a French establishment or is obliged to file French VAT returns.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For tangible exported goods, a 0% French VAT rate applies when the goods leave the European Union territory physically within 90 days of the supply and the exporter retains contemporaneous documentary evidence of the dispatch or transport outside the EU (Article 262 CGI and Articles 74-0 A to 74-0 C of the French VAT annex). For intra-EU supplies of goods to a business customer holding a valid EU VAT identification number and with the goods transported to another Member State, the supply may be zero-rated as an intracommunity supply if the seller has complete Article 289 quinquies declarations and the customer provides its VAT number, with aggregation in the recapitulative sales list (Récapitulatif des Livraisons, DEB). For digitally published video games distributed through Steam and PlayStation Store, the place of supply under Article 58 CGI is where the customer belongs: B2C sales to a French consumer are taxable at 20%; B2C sales to non-EU consumers are outside the scope of French VAT (not merely zero-rated) because the customer is not established in France, and the supplier is not required to use French VAT, although it may be obliged to register and charge VAT in the consumer's foreign jurisdiction. B2B sales of digital content to a French business customer are subject to a reverse-charge mechanism if the supplier is non-established, while B2B sales to a non-French/non-EU business customer using that customer's VAT number or equivalent business registration are outside French VAT. To claim French zero-rating for digital exports, the publisher must demonstrate that the customer is a non-established purchaser with foreign address and, where applicable, a valid foreign VAT registration number, and that the payment card billing address, IP address, device country and bank payment routing are consistent with a foreign destination.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation) filed electronically through the DELTA/DX system, evidenced by the assigned MRN (Movement Reference Number), proving the goods have left the customs territory of the EU
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, or other transport document (CMR/customs consignment note) showing the actual movement of commodities from France to a non-EU destination
Commercial invoice containing the complete description of goods, sale price, terms of delivery and the export VAT zero-rating reference under Article 262 CGI
Packing list and, where relevant, the export accompanying document (DAU-Export) or customs value declaration
Bank transfer receipt / inward remittance certificate (certificat de rapatriement de devises) evidencing full receipt of the export proceeds from the foreign buyer within the statutory period
Foreign buyer registration or VAT number certificate and, where the business customer is a non-EU entity, proof of business nature in the customer's country

For digital store exports, the documentation bundle consists of payment provider transaction logs showing the ultimate payee's billing country, Valve/Steam or PlayStation Store payout statements, geolocation/IP-country logs attached to the consumer's account, purchase confirmation emails, and the platform's VAT report showing that French VAT was not charged on non-French non-EU transactions; no customs declaration is applicable to purely digital supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export and intracommunity zero-rating is subject to intense documentary surveillance by DGFiP's anti-fraud and cross-border divisions. The taxpayer must be able to produce, upon request and without prior notice, all export proof including transport contracts, customs declarations, bank receipts and foreign customer files. If the statutory documentation is incomplete, contradictory, or does not establish the actual dispatch outside the EU, the tax administration retroactively recharacterizes the supply as taxable in France at 20% VAT under Article 271 IV CGI. The assessed VAT is immediately recoverable (clawback) together with late-payment interest calculated at 0.2% per month from the original due date and administrative penalties: a 40% increase for deliberate error or unfounded claim, an 80% increase in cases of abuse of right, dissimulation, destructive concealment or organized tax fraud, and additional penalties up to €750,000 plus a five-year term of imprisonment for criminal tax evasion pursuant to Articles 1729 and 1741 CGI. For fraudulent export schemes, the DGFiP may also apply anti-abuse measures, deny the right to deduct input VAT, issue a tax lien with security measures, initiate criminal proceedings for money laundering if funds are routed offshore, and publish a public notice of fraudulent claims. Refund claims based on export zero-rating are scrutinized by DGFiP's refund unit (Service des Restitutions d'Impôts) and may be suspended until the exporter supplies full digital and documentary evidence, especially for newly registered or high-risk exporters operating through marketplaces and payment aggregators.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (French central bank), exercising supervision and balance-of-payments oversight together with the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) and the Direction Générale du Trésor for foreign-exchange statistics and investment-control purposes
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions under the TFEU free movement of capital regime. France imposes no general exchange-control approval for profit remittance, dividend distribution, or capital repayments. Practical hurdles are limited to anti-money-laundering documentation, verification of beneficial ownership, tax residence certificates, and the absence of EU/UN financial sanctions exposure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement or minimum mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts in France. Digital-platform sales proceeds, including Steam and PlayStation payouts, may be held in foreign currency in a French bank account or converted to euro at market rates at the SARL's discretion. Banks report cross-border flows to Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics via the direct reporting system, but the entity has no separate reporting obligation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: CIC - Crédit Industriel et Commercial S.A.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech electronic-money institutions licensed in France or passporting under PSD2 are legally viable for complementary operational liquidity, but not recommended as the sole treasury rail for a publishing SARL. Providers such as Qonto, Shine, and Blank offer fast onboarding, SEPA Instant, and multi-currency available balance accounts; however, EMIs do not hold a banking license, cannot always provide full SWIFT MT103 participation, and may not support the large inbound capital escrow or notarized share-subscription receipts required for statutory capital. A hybrid stack using a tier-1 bank for capital escrow/long-term clearing and a fintech EMI for day-to-day disbursements is feasible and low risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal statutory requirement that every director appear physically; however, for a SARL with non-resident beneficial owners, tier-1 banks almost uniformly require the statutory manager (gérant) or a legally authorized representative to attend an in-person KYC interview during initial onboarding. Remote account opening is permitted for low-risk domestic structures under Article R.561-12 of the French Monetary and Financial Code using certified copies, electronic identification, and video verification, but foreign shareholders and a cross-border gaming revenue profile materially increase the likelihood that the bank will mandate a physical visit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) or a mismatch between the declared UBO and the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) filing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified RBE extract from the French commercial register (RCS), notarized share-register ledger, corporate organisational chart signed by the gérant, passport or national ID of each UBO, and a sworn declaration of control under Article L.561-2-2 of the French Monetary and Financial Code.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value inbound equity injection from a foreign parent or third-party investor without prior transaction history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letters for the remitter, audited parent company financial statements, source-of-wealth memorandum, minutes of the SARL extraordinary general meeting for the share subscription, evidence of payment of capital tax or registration fees where applicable, and a signed CRS/FATCA self-certification for the new shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large and irregular digital-store payouts from Valve Steam or PlayStation Store flagged as potential unregulated gambling or unlicensed gaming proceeds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current distribution agreements with Valve Corporation and Sony Interactive Entertainment Europe, quarterly platform payout statements, licensing agreements evidencing publishing rights, VAT returns (CA3) matching declared digital sales, and independent auditor's confirmation of the revenue model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media alerts triggered by a shareholder or director in a non-EEA jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions-screening result, government-issued proof of address and identity, professional reference letter from a prior regulated bank, a group compliance attestation, and a complete corporate ownership diagram demonstrating the absence of indirect PEP or embargoed-country involvement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: EUR capital injections for the SARL are routed through the SEPA Credit Transfer scheme using ISO 20022 XML pain.001 messages to the designated corporate IBAN (FR76 + BIC). Non-EUR injections are cleared via SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 pacs.009 with the purpose code 'EQUI' for equity subscription; the narrative must state 'souscription au capital et prime d'émission' and reference the notarial or general-meeting approval. For capital increases exceeding thresholds requiring a statutory auditor, the bank will require a copy of the auditor's report on the capital increase. The receiving bank independently verifies remitter/beneficiary consistency, applies the Banque de France balance-of-payments code for direct investment, and may place funds on a blocking account until full KYC completion.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Royalty and fee payments to EEA licensors or middleware providers are settled by SEPA Credit Transfer. Non-EEA disbursements are cleared via SWIFT MT103 using purpose code 'TRAD' and supported by commercial invoices or contractual schedules. A Commercial Letter of Credit is legally permissible and can be issued by the French bank for high-value engine-source-code escrow or milestone-based advance payments; however, digital-game publishing royalties normally settle clean against invoices and platform payout statements rather than through documentary letters of credit. Steam and PlayStation Store payouts are received on the treasury account through SWIFT or SEPA, reconciled against platform payout reports, and then deployed via the same clearing rails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable FX forwards with maturities aligned to quarterly Steam and PlayStation settlement cycles
EUR/USD FX swaps for temporary liquidity management between the operational account and foreign-currency payout legs
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for subordinate non-convertible or illiquid emerging-market currencies, subject to the entity's documented underlying exposure and bank credit approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Financial Statements (Bilan, Compte de Résultat and Annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and Direction des Services Fiscaux
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 15 April following fiscal year-end (e.g. 15 April for FY ending 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to €7,500; potential judicial dissolution after prolonged non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if annual turnover exceeds €800,000 or balance sheet total exceeds €400,000

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial ownership updates required upon shareholding changes; no mandatory annual confirmation filing unless triggered by transfers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0-4,000 USD (certified audit fee range if mandatory)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate for SMEs with turnover below €7.63 million on first €42,500 profit; R&D tax credit up to 30% of qualifying expenditures; innovation status deductions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1200-A (Déclaration de résultat) filed electronically via impots.gouv.fr

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents, restrict to French-source income only
Limit to French-sourced expenses and permanent establishment costs

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 0.5% of unpaid tax per month of delay, capped at 25% of tax due; possible criminal prosecution for evasion

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 12.8% (reduced to 0% for EU/EEA companies under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and relevant forms to French tax authorities via impots.gouv.fr; apply for reduced rate certificate
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% statutory, reduced under treaties (e.g. 0-10%); Interest: 0% under EU Interest and Royalties Directive and most treaties

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million annual consolidated turnover for Master File/Local File requirements
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France implements Economic Substance Regulations aligned with OECD standards; relevant for holding companies or IP holding entities, but generally applicable to entities with passive income

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or false declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties including fines up to 500,000 euros and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil restitution of evaded taxes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, possible imprisonment, and disqualification from management roles

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a French SARL without real business operations or employees in France
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization as non-resident or denial of deductions; penalties up to 500,000 euros
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil; directors may face civil and criminal sanctions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain adequate TP documentation or apply arm's length principle
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustments by tax authorities increasing taxable base by 10-20%; penalties of 80% of additional tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Potential personal liability if willful misconduct
